issues.reason: 'A participle used as a modifier is an adjective' with the split form as its stated example ('a laminated worktop' → (Member … laminated)), and adjective+noun fusion is licensed only for a recognized kind (term of art, nationality/origin, role title, material adjective) and 'never for incidental description' — participial 'ground' is none of those, so fusing ground_feather violates the stated licence.

new_gaps: a descriptively-modified bare plural inside a rule premise ('ground feathers' as a trigger participant) has no licensed form: the mandated split distributes the modifier per member via an assertion-side rule, and a premise cannot carry a per-member property of a variable group
defect_summary: The split form is mandated — the group typed (GroupOf $f feather) with 'ground' predicated of each member — but a whenever-premise has no licensed carrier for a per-member property of a variable group, so no fully compliant trigger encoding exists; filed as a gap.
notes: The issue's secondary point is weaker — the stated predication test ('the line is part of speech, not meaning') would arguably admit a participial adjective as an exposed genus on a licensed compound — but the fusion bar itself decides the defect.
